newsitem.title: EGYPT: Two girls die in Egypt after illegal circumcision.
newsitem.headline: Two girls die in Egypt after illegal circumcision.

text.p: Two young girls, one four and one three years old, bled to death in southern Egypt after a government doctor tried to circumcise them at their homes, government newspapers said on Wednesday.
The doctor persuaded the fathers to bury the girls in secret and then fled, they said. The local prosecutor has issued a detention order for him to be held for questioning.

In July a decree from Health Minister Ismail Sallam banned the practice of female circumcision, in which the doctor removes some or all of the external genitalia. But the ban has not yet been incorporated into the penal code.
Some human rights activists prefer to call the practice female genital mutilation for the severe form it often takes. Side effects include haemorrhage, shock and sexual dysfunction.
The fathers of the girls, Amira Mahmoud Mohamed, four, and Warda Hussein el-Sayyed, three, had agreed to pay the doctor 10 pounds ($3) each to perform the operation.
The incident took place in the town of Armant, in the Nile valley 520 km (320 miles) south of Cairo. The prosecutor has ordered the bodies of the girls exhumed for examination.
In August an Egyptian doctor in the Nile delta was arrested and charged with negligence after he circumcised a 14-year-old girl. The girl later died.

"We strongly condemn this practice," said Maha Atiyah of the Egyptian Organisation for Human Rights. "We are pressing efforts to pass a law under which a father who does this to girls could be imprisoned for three months."
